q: Night highway check finds women taken for labour. Contractor shows loan thumb papers and says work is voluntary till debt ends. Correct police action?
options: Rescue victims, register trafficking and forced labour case, debt does not justify confinement
Allow work to continue till loan is repaid then release
Impose spot fine on contractor and let vehicle go
Wait for civil court decree before entering vehicle
expl: Loan cannot justify traffic or forced labour. Rescue plus criminal case is mandatory.
why: Forced labour stays illegal even if victim signed paper. SI must prioritize rescue, care and FIR over civil debt.
trapnote: Loan paper never cures bonded labour.

q: A 13-year-old carries chemicals in a fireworks unit for two hours after school. Owner shows parent consent letter. What applies?
options: Unlawful to employ below 14 in hazardous work, consent irrelevant, rescue and prosecute
Lawful because part-time with parental consent
Lawful if wages are paid directly to child
Lawful if child wears mask and gloves
expl: Below 14 barred in factory, mine, hazardous work. Consent or hours do not save it.
why: Protection is absolute for hazardous jobs. SI must stop work and involve Child Welfare Committee.
trapnote: Do not let consent dilute child bar.

q: A man peacefully speaks about his faith door to door without force, fraud or loud abuse. Resident demands total ban on preaching. Correct stand?
options: Allow peaceful profession and spread within order, stop only if force or hatred
Ban all preaching to keep peace
Allow only preaching of majority faith
Arrest preacher for breach of peace at once
expl: Peaceful profess and propagate is protected subject to order, morality, health.
why: Freedom covers inner belief and outward sharing. Police intervene only on coercion or disorder.
trapnote: Peaceful spread is not conversion by force.

q: Panchayat levies Rs 500 on all houses to fund pilgrimage of one community only. Objector refuses. Is levy valid?
options: Invalid if it is a tax to promote one religion, valid only if fee for actual service used
Valid because panchayat decision is final
Valid if amount is small and equal
Invalid even if it is charge for shelter actually used
expl: Compulsory tax for one religion barred. Fee for service used is allowed.
why: Test purpose and return. Tax for faith fails, user charge for facility passes.
trapnote: Tax vs fee turns on service, not amount.

q: A linguistic group speaking a distinct script wants to open a primary school and manage it themselves in their language. Position?
options: Allowed to establish and administer, State may regulate standards without destroying choice
Allowed only if they admit outsiders in majority
Allowed only to establish but not to manage
Not allowed without State adoption of script
expl: Minorities may establish and administer schools. Reasonable regulation allowed.
why: Both legs are needed for claim. State can set excellence norms but not erase minority character.

q: Government orders one-year compulsory disaster service for all youth 18-22 regardless of religion or caste with modest pay. Challenged as forced labour. Result?
options: Valid as compulsory public service imposed equally without discrimination
Invalid as any compulsion is bonded labour
Valid only if only volunteers are taken
Invalid unless paid full market salary
expl: Compulsory public-purpose service without discrimination is an exception.
why: The bar targets exploitation, not equal civic duty. Discrimination would vitiate it.
trapnote: Equal public duty is not begar.

q: Temple trust bars a community from entry citing old custom. Magistrate orders SI to ensure peaceful entry for all. Trust cites religious freedom. Duty?
options: Enforce entry, reform to open public temples overrides exclusionary custom, keep order
Obey trust and block entry to avoid hurt sentiments
Seal temple till custom is decided by priests
Allow entry only on festival off-days
expl: Social reform and temple entry for all classes can override exclusionary custom.
why: Individual and reform power limits group custom. SI enforces lawful entry with dialogue and force protection.

q: A fully State-funded school makes morning prayer of one faith compulsory for all pupils. Parents object. Position?
options: Barred, no religious instruction in wholly State-funded schools
Allowed as discipline and culture
Allowed if majority parents agree
Allowed if prayer is only five minutes
expl: Wholly State-funded schools cannot impart religious instruction.
why: State money means no faith teaching. Consent or majority cannot cure total funding bar.

q: An aided school makes religious instruction compulsory. A 12-year-old is forced without parent nod. School says recognition allows it. Correct?
options: Needs consent, for minor guardian consent, else cannot compel
Recognition alone allows compulsion
Aid allows compulsion without consent
Teacher discretion decides compulsion
expl: In aided-recognised schools compulsion needs consent, guardian for minor.
why: Aid does not equal ownership. Consent protects conscience of child and parent.
trapnote: Aided needs consent, funded bars fully.

q: Parliament by law limits political activities of armed forces members to keep discipline. Member claims free speech violation. Result?
options: Restriction valid if by Parliament law for forces discipline
Invalid as rights are absolute for all
Valid even if ordered by local commander orally
Invalid unless State assembly also approves
expl: Parliament may restrict forces rights for discipline and duty.
why: Uniformed duty needs special restraint. Law must come from Parliament, not executive whim.

q: Town charges Rs 200 pilgrim shelter cleaning fee from users vs Rs 200 general levy on all to promote one festival. Which is which?
options: User charge for service is fee and allowed, general levy for one faith is tax and barred
Both are taxes and both barred
Both are fees and both allowed
Small levies are always allowed
expl: Fee needs service quid pro quo. Tax for one religion fails.
why: Look at return benefit. Service users pay fee validly, all residents cannot be taxed for one faith.
trapnote: Service link decides fee vs tax.

q: Compare three schools: fully State-paid, old endowment for faith now State-managed, private aided. Which rule fits?
options: Fully paid barred, endowment exception may continue, aided needs consent
All three can compel prayer equally
All three are fully barred
Aided is barred but fully paid can compel
expl: Funding source decides rule. Endowment trust is the narrow exception.
why: Do not mix buckets. Total funding bars, trust history saves, aid triggers consent.

q: Group A has distinct script and wants to conserve it. Group B claims special right to run colleges with autonomy. Who claims what?
options: Any cultural section may conserve, only religious-linguistic minority runs institutions specially
Both claims need minority status
Both claims are open to any group
Neither claim exists
expl: Culture claim is wide, school autonomy claim needs minority status.
why: Conservation is for any section. Establish-administer is a narrower minority shield.
trapnote: Wide culture vs narrow school right.

q: A distinct religious sect manages its rituals and temple funds vs an individual preaches peacefully. How do their freedoms differ?
options: Sect manages religious affairs as group subject to order, individual professes subject to same limits plus reform
Sect is absolute, individual is barred
Individual is absolute, sect has no right
Both are absolute without limits
expl: Group management and individual practice both limited by order, health, morality.
why: No freedom is absolute. Group gets institutional limb, individual gets conscience limb.

q: Four petitions: detained person not produced, officer refuses legal duty, trial court exceeds power, unqualified man holds public post. Match relief by function.
options: Produce person, order duty done, stop excess, question authority in that order
Order duty, produce person, question authority, stop excess
Stop excess for all four
Question authority for all four
expl: Functions map to produce, command duty, restrain, test title.
why: Learn writs by action. Detention needs production, inaction needs command, excess needs restraint.

q: Consider: I. State can never impose compulsory service. II. It can if for public purpose without discrimination. III. Forced labour for private master is barred. Which are correct?
options: II and III only, I uses absolute never and is false
I, II and III all correct
I and III only
Only I correct
expl: Absolute never is trap. Equal public service is allowed, private forced labour barred.
why: Statement I overstates. The exception saves equal civic duty while banning exploitation.

q: Consider: I. Tax for one religion barred. II. Fee for service used is also always barred. III. Endowed faith school managed by State may continue teaching. Correct?
options: I and III only, II is half-truth confusing fee with tax
I, II, III all correct
II and III only
Only II correct
expl: Fee with service is allowed. Half-truth equates fee with tax.
why: Statement II looks correct but drops service link. Endowment exception keeps III alive.

q: Consider: I. Minority must both set up and run institution. II. On compulsory takeover fair compensation needed. III. General college quota law skips minority colleges. Correct?
options: I, II and III all correct
Only I correct
I and II only, III is false
II and III only
expl: Twin requirement plus compensation plus exclusion from general quota all hold.
why: All three limbs complete the shield. Miss one leg and autonomy claim weakens.

q: Consider: I. Only Parliament punishes for these freedoms. II. Parliament can limit forces rights. III. Parliament can indemnify martial law acts. Correct?
options: I, II and III all correct, exclusivity is deliberate
Only II correct
I and II only
II and III only, I belongs to States
expl: Punishment, forces curbs, martial law cover all vest only in Parliament.
why: One national standard is intended. States cannot legislate on these heads.

q: Consider: I. Below 14 hazardous work barred even with consent. II. Aided school cannot deny admission on religion alone. III. Victim consent justifies trafficking. Correct?
options: I and II only, III confuses consent with freedom
I, II, III all correct
II and III only
Only III correct
expl: Consent never justifies trafficking. Other two protect child and pupil.
why: Trafficking consent is legally void due to coercion. Child bar and admission guard stand.
